faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's lightest overhead stirrer, used for stirring media that a magnetic stirrer cannot turn. It delivers 65 Ncm of torque across 20 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 10,000 mPas or volumes up to 25 litres in water.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is 65 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, is the specification that determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer stir 25 litres of a viscous medium?
faqs.answer: No. The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 10,000 mPas or volumes up to 25 litres in water. These are two separate ceilings on the same 65 Ncm drive, not a combined capability.

faqs.question: What viscosity can the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 10,000 mPas, at reduced volume. This is well beyond the point at which a magnetic stir bar decouples and stops turning.

faqs.question: What is included with the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is supplied as a drive unit. The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 0.5 mm to 10.5 mm in diameter. It is keyless, so no tool is needed to change a stirring element.

faqs.question: What is the Max button on the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Max button on the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer takes the drive to its maximum speed of 2,000 rpm immediately. It is designed for short bursts, such as reslurrying a settled suspension or distributing a component that has just been added to the medium.

faqs.question: What happens if the Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer is overloaded?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Core with RS232 Overhead Stirrer has automatic overload cut-out, which stops the motor rather than letting it stall under strain. The motor is also monitored in software, and a fault produces an error message.

The Hei-Torque Expert-100 Overhead Stirrer delivers 100 Ncm of torque with a live torque trend display, for viscosities to 60,000 mPas.
Most stirring is a black box. You set a speed, you come back later, and you hope the medium did what you expected.

features: Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque reliably monitored. This is the feature that turns a stirrer into an instrument that tells you something.
100 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 100 Ncm the Expert reaches media six times more viscous than the Hei-TORQUE Core.
Viscosity to 60,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 60,000 mPas. That covers thick suspensions, gels, and viscous polymer solutions that a lighter drive would simply stall in.

Speed from 10 rpm: The range starts at 10 rpm, lower than the Core's 20 rpm. A viscous medium often needs to be brought up gently, and a drive that cannot go slow enough is as much a problem as one that cannot go fast enough.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.
Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in demanding media.
90 W Power Input: Despite delivering more torque than the Hei-TORQUE Core, the Expert draws less power, at 90 W against the Core's 105 W.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

Polymerisation: Rising torque is the signal that the medium is thickening.
Dissolution and Suspension: Falling torque indicates solids going into solution.
Fume Hood Work: IP54 and under 50 dB(A), sealed and quiet enough for enclosed working.
Reactor Superstructures: Rated as a drive for reactor assemblies.

features: 200 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 200 Ncm the Expert 200 turns media that would stall a 100 Ncm drive, and it does so at the same working volume.
Viscosity to 100,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 100,000 mPas. That is the territory of heavy gels, pastes, loaded slurries and viscous polymer solutions, where a lighter drive simply stops.

Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run. Changes in the medium can be tracked as they happen, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored reliably. At this end of the viscosity range, headroom is what you are watching.

Speed from 10 rpm: The range starts at 10 rpm. A very viscous medium usually needs to be brought up slowly, and a drive that cannot go slow enough is as much of a problem as one that cannot go fast enough.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.

Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped. At 200 Ncm, a tool that slips in the chuck is not a minor inconvenience.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in demanding media.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.

Polymerisation: Rising torque is the direct signal that the medium is thickening.
Heavily Loaded Slurries: High solids loading raises torque demand sharply.
Monitored Reactions: The torque trend display shows the medium changing as it happens.
Fume Hood Work: IP54 and under 50 dB(A), sealed and quiet enough for enclosed working.

Gentle Start on Heavy Media: The 10 rpm minimum brings a viscous medium up slowly.

It delivers 200 Ncm of torque across 10 to 2,000 rpm, for viscosities up to 100,000 mPas or volumes up to 50 litres in water, and displays the delivered torque live.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer is 200 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-100 and the Expert-200?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 delivers 200 Ncm against the Expert-100's 100 Ncm, and reaches 100,000 mPas against 60,000 mPas. The maximum volume is the same on both, at 50 litres in water. The extra torque buys a thicker medium, not a larger vessel.

faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer handles viscosities up to 100,000 mPas, at reduced volume. That covers heavy gels, pastes, loaded slurries, and viscous polymer solutions.

faqs.question: What is the torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Expert-200 Overhead Stirrer?

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer is the top of the Expert range, with a two-gear drive delivering 400 Ncm, for viscosities to 250,000 mPas and volumes to 100 litres in water.
The two lower Experts stall at the same 50 litre volume no matter how much torque you add. This one breaks that limit, because it does not just add torque. It adds a gearbox.
The only Expert with two gears. Gear I trades speed for torque and delivers full power below 400 rpm. Gear II opens up to 2,000 rpm for thinner media.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Two-Gear Transmission: The Expert 400 is the only model in the Expert range with two gears. Gear I concentrates the drive's power in the speed range up to 400 rpm, which is where highly viscous media must be mixed. Gear II runs up to 2,000 rpm for lighter work. One drive covers both regimes, which a single-gear stirrer cannot.

400 Ncm of Torque: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. At 400 Ncm this is the most powerful drive in the Expert range, built for media that stall everything below it.

Viscosity to 250,000 mPas: The drive handles media up to 250,000 mPas, more than double the Expert 200. This is the territory of stiff pastes, heavy adhesives, and loaded slurries that behave more like solids than liquids.

Volume to 100 Litres: The maximum volume is 100 litres in water, double the two lower Experts. This is the only model in the Expert range that raises the volume ceiling, not just the viscosity ceiling.

Torque Trend Display: A bar indicator keeps the delivered torque visible for the whole run, so changes in the medium can be tracked, the speed adjusted in response, and the peak torque monitored. At 400 Ncm, watching the headroom matters.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.

Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely. At 400 Ncm, a tool that slips in the chuck is a serious hazard, and the safety ring is there to prevent it.
2.4 Inch Display: Application parameters are set and the process controlled from a 2.4 inch display, including the torque trend bar and the gear selection.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs in the demanding media this model is built for.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.
applications: Very High-Viscosity Media: 400 Ncm drives a shaft through media up to 250,000 mPas.
Stiff Pastes and Adhesives: Gear I delivers full torque at the low speeds these media require.
Large-Volume Mixing: Up to 100 litres in water, double the lower Experts.
Loaded Slurries: High solids loading demands both torque and low-speed control.
Monitored Reactions: The torque trend display shows the medium changing as it happens.
Low-Speed High-Torque Mixing: Gear I is built specifically for this regime.
Fume Hood Work: IP54 and under 50 dB(A), sealed and quiet enough for enclosed working.
Reactor Superstructures: Rated as a drive for reactor assemblies.
Continuous Stirring: Rated for continuous operation, with a certificate available.

faqs.question: What is the two-gear design on the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer?

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-200 and the Expert-400?

faqs.question: What is the torque trend display on the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer?

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Expert-400 Overhead Stirrer be used in a fume hood?

products.overview:
The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer is the connected, programmable Hei-TORQUE, delivering 100 Ncm with ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, and free Hei-Control software.
The Ultimate 100 stirs exactly what the Expert 100 stirs: same torque, same viscosity, same volume. What you are buying is not more power. It is the ability to program, connect, and document.
Programmable methods. Ramp programming lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly, run after run, operator after operator.
The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are NOT included.
features: Ramp Programming: Ramp programming lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly. A method written into the drive is a method that runs the same way every time, regardless of who is operating it. This is the single feature that separates the Ultimate line from the Expert line.

USB and RS232 Interfaces: Two interfaces connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager. This is what lets an overhead stirrer become a controlled step in an automated process rather than a manual interruption in one.

Free Hei-Control Software: The scope of delivery includes the free Hei-Control software, which remotely controls up to four devices from a single PC. Remote control and data logging are quick to set up, at no extra cost.

Process Monitoring and Documentation: The drive reads out the torque trend as a value and includes a timer function, giving you the equipment to document your application parameters. A number can be recorded and audited; a bar on a screen cannot.

Torque to 100 Ncm: Torque, not speed, decides whether an overhead stirrer can do your job. The Ultimate 100 delivers 100 Ncm, for viscosities up to 60,000 mPas, the same working envelope as the Expert 100.

Change of Rotational Direction: Rotation runs clockwise or counterclockwise. The flow variation makes it easier to stir up suspensions and accelerates dissolution processes, which a single-direction drive cannot do.

Controllable Start-Up: After switch-on, the start-up intensity is adjustable from soft to fast. That lets you choose the right ramp for the application and prevents liquid from splashing at the start.

Safety Start and Stop Touch Function: Starting or stopping is a swipe along the control panel. It works reliably through gloves, and it cannot be triggered accidentally by a knock, a sleeve, or a passing hand.
Quick-Action Chuck with Safety Ring: The chuck opens and closes by hand with no tools, and the safety ring holds the stirring tool securely once clamped.
Built for Fume Hoods and Reactor Superstructures: At IP54 and under 50 dB(A), the drive is sealed and quiet enough to work inside a fume hood, and it is rated as a drive for reactor superstructures.
Automatic Overload Cut-Out with Display: If the load exceeds what the drive can deliver, the motor cuts out automatically and the display tells you why.
KTY Motor Temperature Monitoring: The motor temperature is monitored directly, which protects the drive during long runs.
Suitable for Continuous Operation: The duty cycle permits continuous operation, and a certificate for continuous operation is available for the Hei-TORQUE range.
applications: Automated Laboratory Processes: USB and RS232 connect the drive to a PLC or automation system.
Documented Methods: Torque trend as a value and a timer support recording application parameters.
Reproducible Stirring: Ramp programming repeats a defined profile exactly.
Remote and Multi-Device Control: Hei-Control software runs up to four devices from one PC.
Suspensions: Bidirectional rotation stirs up settled solids.
Dissolution: Reversing the flow accelerates dissolution processes.
Fume Hood Work: IP54 and under 50 dB(A), sealed and quiet enough for enclosed working.
Reactor Superstructures: Rated as a drive for reactor assemblies.
Continuous Stirring: Rated for continuous operation, with a certificate available.

faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 and the Expert-100 share the same drive: 100 Ncm, 60,000 mPas, 50 litres in water, and the same chassis. faqs.question: What is the Hei-Control software included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: Hei-Control is the free software included in the scope of delivery of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer. It provides remote control and data logging, and can control up to four devices from a single PC.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer be programmed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer offers ramp programming, which lets you define a stirring profile and repeat it exactly. This is the main capability that distinguishes the Ultimate line from the Expert line.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-100 Overhead Stirrer is 100 Ncm. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer used for?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer is Heidolph's most powerful overhead stirrer, a programmable two-gear drive used for very high-viscosity media, large volumes, and automated documented processes. It delivers 400 Ncm for viscosities up to 250,000 mPas or volumes up to 100 litres in water, with USB and RS232 interfaces and free Hei-Control software.

faqs.question: What is the maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The maximum torque of the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer is 400 Ncm, the highest in the Hei-TORQUE range. Torque, rather than speed, determines whether an overhead stirrer can turn a given medium.

faqs.question: What is the two-gear design on the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer has a two-gear drive. Gear I runs from 10 to 400 rpm and concentrates the full torque at low speed, where highly viscous media must be stirred. Gear II runs from 20 to 2,000 rpm for thinner media.

faqs.question: What viscosity and volume can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer handle?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer reaches viscosities up to 250,000 mPas or volumes up to 100 litres in water, the highest figures in the range. These are two ends of one working envelope, so a very viscous medium is turned in a smaller volume.

faqs.question: Can the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer be programmed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer offers ramp programming with a favourites memory, letting you store time-dependent stirring profiles and rerun them exactly, along with a timer for reproducible process times.

faqs.question: What interfaces does the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer have?
faqs.answer: The Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer has two interfaces, USB and RS232, which connect the drive to a PC, a programmable logic controller, or an automation system such as LabManager.

faqs.question: What is the Hei-Control software included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: Hei-Control is the free software included in the scope of delivery. It provides remote control and data logging, and can control up to four devices from a single PC.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the Hei-Torque Expert-400 and the Ultimate-400?
faqs.answer: Both use the same two-gear 400 Ncm drive, with the same 250,000 mPas and 100 litre limits. The Ultimate-400 adds ramp programming, USB and RS232 interfaces, free Hei-Control software for up to four devices, and a torque trend read out as a documentable value. The Expert-400 offers the drive without the programming and connectivity, for processes run by hand.

faqs.question: What shaft diameters fit the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?
faqs.answer: The quick-action chuck on the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer accepts stirring shafts from 2.5 mm to 10.5 mm, and has a safety ring. At 400 Ncm the shaft must also be rated for the torque.

faqs.question: What is included with the Hei-Torque Ultimate-400 Overhead Stirrer?

The stand, boss head, stirring shaft, and stirring element are separate items and are not included. At 400 Ncm the stand, boss head, and shaft must all be rated for the reaction torque, so Inkarp quotes a complete working setup rated for the load.

sections.title: Torque, Viscosity and Volume Planning
body: Torque, viscosity and volume planning sets out what the Ultimate 400's two-gear drive delivers, and why the gearbox is what reaches both ceilings.

The drive reaches 250,000 mPas and 100 litres in water, the highest figures in the range, and the reason is the transmission rather than raw torque alone. Torque is hardest to deliver at low speed, and low speed is exactly where a very viscous medium has to be stirred. Gear I concentrates the full 400 Ncm below 400 rpm to meet that; Gear II opens up to 2,000 rpm once the work is thinner.

The viscosity and volume figures are the two ends of one envelope rather than a pair that holds at once: the full 250,000 mPas applies at reduced volume, the full 100 litres at low viscosity. The torque readout shows, in real time, where within that envelope a given setup is running.
Product expert note Share your medium, its viscosity, your working volume, and your vessel diameter, and our team will confirm the gear your process runs in and that 400 Ncm suits the job.
